passage:
A city created an online map of every public tree. Each tree had information about its species, age, health, and care schedule.
Residents could report broken branches or disease through the map. Students used it for science projects. Artists used it to design walking tours.
Before the map, trees were part of the background. After the map, people began noticing them as individuals.
Some residents even checked "their" street trees after storms.
The project showed how data can create care. When a tree becomes a point on a map with a name and history, it is harder to treat it as invisible.
